title: Smacafam Trentino
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A rustic Trentino buckwheat cake studded with crumbled sausage, its playful name literally meaning 'hunger killer,' a hearty savory bake meant to satisfy a very hungry table.
longDesc: Smacafam's dense, buckwheat-based batter is poured directly over crumbled sausage before baking, resulting in something between a savory cake and a thick pancake, exactly the kind of filling, no-fuss dish its blunt name promises.
ingredients: 80 g (⅓ cup) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour, milk, and eggs together into a smooth, thin batter.
Season with salt and pepper and whisk in the melted butter.
Lightly brown the crumbled sausage in a skillet, just to render some fat, without fully cooking through.
Butter a round baking pan and scatter the partially cooked sausage evenly across the bottom.
Pour the batter over the sausage.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 35–40 minutes until set and golden on top.
Let rest for a few minutes before slicing into wedges and serving hot.
chefTips: Only partially cook the sausage before baking, as it finishes cooking through in the oven.
The batter should be quite thin, similar to a thick crepe or pancake batter.
This is a genuinely hearty, filling dish, true to its blunt "hunger killer" name.
commonMistakes: Fully cooking the sausage beforehand, which can dry it out by the time the whole dish finishes baking.
Making the batter too thick, resulting in a denser, less traditional texture.
Underbaking, leaving the center too wet and unset.
servedWith: A light red wine from Trentino
reheating: Reheat gently in the oven until warmed through.
healthBenefits: Buckwheat provides fiber and is naturally gluten-free as a grain, though this dish includes wheat-containing sausage.
culturalNote: Smacafam's blunt, practical name reflects its role as a genuinely hearty, filling dish in Trentino's mountain kitchens, meant to satisfy hungry families after a long day.
